To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the N-terminal repeat domains of AtClp C1 and AtClpd are highly divergent from each other.
the N-terminal domain (NTD) of ClpC is highly divergent from ClpD in plants.
the N-terminal repeat domain of AtClpd1 has divergent structural organization and could be activated by Cyclomarin A.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural analysis of AtClp proteins which could be useful to gain insights into the molecular mechanism of the chaperone function and the role of Clp proteins during plant stress conditions.

the structural characterization of the plant specific ClpD protein and its comparison with ClpC1, which could be a starting point for further studies on the role of ClpC and its homolog ClpD in plant stress response.
the structural characterization of the NTDs of two Clp chaperone proteins from A. thaliana and their comparative analysis with other known Clp chaptone proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AtClpC and AtClpC have a distinct role in the plant stress response.
AtClpD could be a unique chaperone with a distinct structural organization and function.
the AtClpD protein, despite its similarity to AtClpC in sequence, is structurally different and could have a distinct functional role.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NTD of AtClp proteins have distinct features and are likely to have specific roles.
the structural organization of AtClpN-terminal domain has diverged significantly from other Clp chaperone proteins and could be a key factor for their functional specificity.
, AtClpC and AtClpC have diverged in their NTDs, which is a region that is important for their adaptor interactions and regulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the NTD of AtClp D has a divergent structure compared to any known bacterial or plant ClpC, and this could be the reason for the functional specialization of AtClp C1 and AtClpd during plant stress conditions.
